name: adPEAS - AD Privilege Escalation Awesome Script
description: adPEAS automates Active Directory enumeration for privilege escalation. It checks for Kerberoastable/AS-REP roastable accounts, ADCS misconfigurations (ESC1-ESC8), delegation abuse, GPO weaknesses, LAPS, gMSA, credential exposure, and more. Think of it as linPEAS but specifically for AD domain escalation paths.
notes:
=== DOWNLOAD & RUN ===
  # Download
  iex(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/61106960/adPEAS/main/adPEAS.ps1")
  # Or from disk:
  Import-Module .\adPEAS.ps1
  Invoke-adPEAS

=== SPECIFIC MODULES ===
  Invoke-adPEAS -Module Domain       # Domain info
  Invoke-adPEAS -Module Creds        # Credential exposure
  Invoke-adPEAS -Module Delegation   # Delegation abuse
  Invoke-adPEAS -Module Accounts     # Kerberoast/ASREP
  Invoke-adPEAS -Module Computer     # LAPS, gMSA, RBCD
  Invoke-adPEAS -Module ADCS         # Certificate services
  Invoke-adPEAS -Module BloodHound   # BH collection

=== WHAT IT CHECKS ===
- Kerberoastable accounts (SPNs)
- AS-REP roastable accounts
- Unconstrained/constrained/RBCD delegation
- ADCS ESC1-ESC8 vulnerabilities
- LAPS configuration
- gMSA password access
- GPO abuse paths
- Credential in description fields
- AdminSDHolder persistence
- Trust relationships

recommended.note: SharpView for manual enumeration; adPEAS automates the common checks.

defense.why_it_works: adPEAS uses standard LDAP queries and PowerShell AD modules to enumerate privilege escalation paths. All checks use legitimate AD query interfaces that domain users have access to by default.
defense.prerequisites: Domain user credentials; PowerShell execution on a domain-joined machine.
defense.impact: Reveals all common AD privilege escalation paths in one run; accelerates domain compromise.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1087.002] High volume of LDAP queries from a single source; PowerShell script block logging showing adPEAS module.
defense.artifacts: PowerShell script block logs (4104) with adPEAS functions; LDAP query volume spike; Sysmon pipe/network events.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=4104 ScriptBlockText="*adPEAS*"
| table _time, ComputerName, UserName, ScriptBlockText
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4104
| where CommandLine has "adPEAS"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, CommandLine
defense.prevention: PowerShell Constrained Language Mode; script block logging; AMSI; restrict unnecessary LDAP query permissions.

detections.name: adPEAS AD enumeration script execution
detections.logic:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "PowerShellCommand"
| where AdditionalFields has "adPEAS" or AdditionalFields has "Invoke-adPEAS"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AdditionalFields
detections.false_positives: Authorized security assessments; internal red team exercises
detections.tuning: Alert on any detection; whitelist only during authorized assessments
